Struct Triangle

Represents a triangle defined by three vertices in 2D space. The vertices should be arranged in counter-clockwise order for proper geometric calculations.

public readonly struct Triangle : IEquatable<Triangle>, IShapeTypeProvider, IClosedShapeTypeProvider

Remarks

This structure provides comprehensive functionality for triangle operations including geometric calculations, shape conversions, containment tests, intersections, and various utility methods for working with triangular geometry. The triangle is immutable and all operations that modify the triangle return a new instance.

Constructors

Triangle(Vector2, Segment)

Initializes a new triangle using a point and a line segment, ensuring counter-clockwise vertex ordering.

public Triangle(Vector2 p, Segment s)

Parameters

p Vector2

The third vertex of the triangle.

s Segment

The line segment that forms one edge of the triangle.

Remarks

This constructor automatically determines the proper vertex ordering to ensure the triangle has counter-clockwise orientation by using the cross product to determine which side of the segment the point lies on.

Triangle(Vector2, Vector2, Vector2)

Initializes a new triangle with three specified vertices.

public Triangle(Vector2 a, Vector2 b, Vector2 c)

Parameters

a Vector2

The first vertex of the triangle.

b Vector2

The second vertex of the triangle.

c Vector2

The third vertex of the triangle.

Remarks

The vertices should be specified in counter-clockwise order for proper geometric calculations. Clockwise ordering may cause unexpected results in some operations that depend on triangle orientation.

ContainsPoint(Vector2)

Determines whether the triangle contains the specified point.

public bool ContainsPoint(Vector2 p)

Parameters

p Vector2

The point to test for containment.

Returns

bool

True if the point is inside or on the boundary of the triangle; otherwise, false.

Remarks

This method uses the cross product method to determine point containment by checking that the point is on the same side of all three triangle edges. This assumes the triangle vertices are in counter-clockwise order for proper containment testing. Points on the triangle's edges are considered to be contained within the triangle.

DrawGappedOutline(float, LineDrawingInfo, GappedOutlineDrawingInfo)

Draws a gapped outline for a triangle, creating a dashed or segmented effect along the triangle's perimeter.

public float DrawGappedOutline(float perimeter, LineDrawingInfo lineInfo, GappedOutlineDrawingInfo gapDrawingInfo)

Parameters

perimeter float

The total length of the triangle's perimeter. If zero or negative, the method calculates it automatically. Providing a known length avoids redundant calculations and improves performance, especially for static segments.

lineInfo LineDrawingInfo

Parameters describing how to draw the outline.

gapDrawingInfo GappedOutlineDrawingInfo

Parameters describing the gap configuration.

Returns

float

The perimeter of the triangle if positive; otherwise, -1. If the shape does not change, the valid length can be reused in subsequent frames to avoid recalculating.

Remarks

  • If gapDrawingInfo.Gaps.Gaps is 0 or gapDrawingInfo.GapPerimeterPercentage.GapPerimeterPercentage is 0, the outline is drawn solid.
  • If gapDrawingInfo.GapPerimeterPercentage.GapPerimeterPercentage is 1 or greater, no outline is drawn.

DrawVertices(float, ColorRgba, float)

Draws circles at each vertex of the triangle.

public void DrawVertices(float vertexRadius, ColorRgba color, float smoothness)

Parameters

vertexRadius float

The radius of each vertex circle.

color ColorRgba

The color of the vertex circles.

smoothness float

The smoothness value (0-1). This controls the visual quality of the circle by inversely interpolating the current CircleSideLengthRange. A value of 0 uses the maximum side length (fewer sides, less smooth), while 1 uses the minimum side length (more sides, smoother). The resulting side length determines the number of polygon sides used to approximate the circle.

GetArea()

Calculates the area of the triangle using the cross product method.

public float GetArea()

Returns

float

The area of the triangle in square units.

Remarks

This method uses the cross product formula for efficiency and numerical stability. The result is always positive regardless of vertex ordering.

GetAreaHeron()

Calculates the triangle area using Heron's formula (based on side lengths).

public float GetAreaHeron()

Returns

float

The area of the triangle in square units. Returns 0 for degenerate triangles (invalid or zero-area).

Remarks

Computes side lengths from the triangle's edges and applies: area = sqrt(s * (s - a) * (s - b) * (s - c)), where s is the semi-perimeter. For numerical stability in many cases, prefer GetArea().

GetBoundingBox()

Calculates and returns the axis-aligned bounding rectangle that completely contains this triangle.

public Rect GetBoundingBox()

Returns

Rect

A rectangle that represents the smallest axis-aligned bounding box containing all triangle vertices.

Remarks

The bounding box is useful for broad-phase collision detection and spatial partitioning algorithms.

GetCentroid()

Calculates and returns the centroid (geometric center) of the triangle.

public Vector2 GetCentroid()

Returns

Vector2

The centroid point, which is the average of all three vertices.

Remarks

The centroid is the point where the triangle would balance if it were a physical object of uniform density. It is always located inside the triangle, regardless of the triangle's shape.

GetCircumCircle()

Calculates and returns the circumcircle of the triangle.

public Circle GetCircumCircle()

Returns

Circle

A circle that passes through all three vertices of the triangle.

Remarks

The circumcircle is the unique circle that passes through all three vertices of the triangle. This is particularly useful in Delaunay triangulation algorithms and various geometric computations. The calculation uses the determinant method for numerical stability.

float

The inradius as a positive float; returns 0 if the triangle is degenerate or has zero area.

result Points

Returns

Points

GetInterpolatedEdgePoints(float, int)

Gets interpolated points by performing multiple steps of edge interpolation, creating a fractal-like effect.

public Points GetInterpolatedEdgePoints(float t, int steps)

Parameters

t float

The interpolation factor (0.0 to 1.0) to apply at each step.

steps int

The number of interpolation steps to perform.

Returns

Points

A collection of three points after performing the specified number of interpolation steps.

Remarks

This method repeatedly applies edge interpolation, where each step uses the results of the previous step. With multiple steps, this creates a spiral-like or fractal pattern moving toward the triangle's interior. If steps is 1 or less, this behaves the same as the single-parameter version.

ProjectShape(Polygon, Vector2, bool)

Projects this triangle along the given vector and writes the convex hull of the combined point set into result.

public bool ProjectShape(Polygon result, Vector2 v, bool useBuffer = false)

Parameters

result Polygon

The destination polygon that receives the convex hull of the original and projected triangle vertices.

v Vector2

The vector along which to project the triangle.

useBuffer bool

true to reuse the internal points buffer and avoid a temporary allocation; false to allocate a new temporary buffer. Set this to false when calling from parallel or multi-threaded code, since the internal buffer is shared and not thread-safe.

Returns

bool

true if v is non-zero and result was populated; otherwise, false.

Remarks

This method constructs a temporary six-point set containing the triangle vertices and those same vertices translated by v, then computes the convex hull into result.

ProjectShape(Vector2, bool)

Projects the triangle along a vector to create a convex hull polygon.

public Polygon? ProjectShape(Vector2 v, bool useBuffer = false)

Parameters

v Vector2

The vector along which to project the triangle.

useBuffer bool

true to reuse the internal points buffer and avoid a temporary allocation; false to allocate a new temporary buffer. Set this to false when calling from parallel or multi-threaded code, since the internal buffer is shared and not thread-safe.

Returns

Polygon

A convex polygon representing the projected shape, or null if the vector has zero length.

Remarks

This method creates a shadow-like projection by extruding the triangle along the vector and computing the convex hull of all resulting points.

Triangulate(Triangulation, int)

Triangulates this triangle by adding random interior points and performing point-cloud triangulation into result.

public void Triangulate(Triangulation result, int pointCount)

Parameters

result Triangulation

The destination triangulation that will be cleared and populated with the generated triangles.

pointCount int

The number of random interior points to add before triangulation.

Remarks

If pointCount is negative, result receives only this triangle. Otherwise, the triangle vertices and the generated interior points are passed to TriangulatePointCloud. Random points are generated using barycentric coordinates so they lie inside the triangle.

Triangulate(Triangulation, Vector2)

Triangulates this triangle using the specified point as an interior vertex and writes the result into result.

public void Triangulate(Triangulation result, Vector2 p)

Parameters

result Triangulation

The destination triangulation that will be cleared and populated with the generated sub-triangles.

p Vector2

The interior point to use for triangulation.

Remarks

The resulting triangulation contains three triangles: A-B-P, B-C-P, and C-A-P. This method does not verify that the point is actually inside the triangle. Only valid triangles (area > 0) are added to result.

Triangulate(Triangulation, float)

Recursively subdivides this triangle into smaller triangles until each resulting triangle has an area less than or equal to minArea.

public bool Triangulate(Triangulation result, float minArea)

Parameters

result Triangulation

The destination triangulation that will be cleared and populated with the generated triangles.

minArea float

The maximum allowed area for each resulting triangle. Must be greater than 0.

Returns

bool

true if triangulation succeeds; otherwise, false when minArea is less than or equal to 0.

Remarks

Larger triangles are split using random interior points until all generated triangles satisfy the area threshold. Only triangles with positive area are included in the output.
